topic: For finite-state, finite-action stationary iid-response SCMs with a known nominal controlled transition law whose positive cells are at least epsilon, fixed factual and alternative policies, an arbitrary observation map, bounded rewards, and a nominal target-policy Poisson solution of span at most B, study the sharp interval of the same unit's conditional counterfactual average reward after a factual record of length T. Prove an explicit C(d,k,epsilon,B)/sqrt(T) upper bound on the expected interval diameter uniformly over the complete compatible canonical-response polytope, without imposing a lower bound on response masses or contraction of every conditional counterfactual kernel. Prove sharpness using the legal full-support binary feedback construction, give attained exact finite response-program endpoints, and provide honest simultaneous confidence-fiber coverage when the nominal transition law is estimated from independent calibration data. Do not claim recordwise shrinkage or apply the result to absorbing targets that violate the Poisson condition. PRESOLVE EVIDENCE REQUIRING VERIFICATION: A conditional Poisson decomposition yields an explicit O(sqrt(log T/T)) whole-class bound; all 28 binary antipodal segments admit a uniform expected-diameter bound of 180/sqrt(T) by endpoint linearity, Abel-Doob arguments, and integrable geometric-Walsh derivative energy; exact checks validate the positive feedback witness, hidden-HMM recursion, and derivative identities. UNRESOLVED BOTTLENECK: Prove the root-T martingale-family maximal inequality uniformly over the entire higher-dimensional response polytope; the solved edges do not control arbitrary mixtures. EARLY KILL TEST: Analyze the explicit synchronizer/two-permutation triangle over its full two-dimensional parameter square and either prove a T-independent root-T bound or exhibit a legal T-dependent selection with divergent normalized width; conditional-positivity assumptions do not pass. STRONGEST-FORM DRAFT (unverified, gaps listed inside): <repo-root>/internal/presolve_drafts/scm_longrecord_counterfactual_ambiguity_rate.md.

open_problems.open_problem: Decide whether the expected diameter of the sharp same-unit conditional average-reward interval is uniformly at most C(d,k,epsilon,B)/sqrt(T) over the complete stationary compatible canonical-response polytope, or whether a legal T-dependent response-law sequence makes its root-T normalized width diverge.

open_problems.why_unsolved: Published results separately provide sharp one-step compatible-SCM bounds, finite canonical response representations, and Poisson-martingale concentration for one fixed kernel. The closest prior SCM proposal explicitly allowed stage-specific response tables, and a reviewer left the growing-information width frontier open. With one response-mass vector reused through feedback, factual conditioning produces a continuum of posterior-normalized Poisson martingales whose optimizer depends on the record; response masses may vanish, so neither a uniform likelihood denominator nor per-kernel contraction is available. The missing proof step is a T-independent maximal inequality for this whole polytope-indexed family; bounds on the 28 binary edges do not control interior mixtures.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: Either a theorem proving E[diam I_T] <= C(d,k,epsilon,B)/sqrt(T) uniformly over all compatible stationary response laws, with a legal full-support binary construction giving a matching c/sqrt(T) lower bound, or an explicit compatible sequence q_T for which sqrt(T)E[diam I_T] diverges while the Poisson-span condition holds.

writing_exemplar.why: Its motivation distinguishes robust bounds over all compatible causal mechanisms from answers under an arbitrarily selected mechanism.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: A known controlled transition law leaves its SCM unidentified -> compatible mechanisms disagree on same-unit counterfactuals -> sharp optimization replaces mechanism selection -> ask whether a long factual record shrinks this ambiguity at a uniform rate

method_exemplars.technique: Carry over the average-reward Poisson decomposition into bounded terminal bias plus martingale differences and its nonasymptotic concentration proof.
method_exemplars.why_closest: The desired root-T bound has the same bounded-bias additive-functional structure, but the proof must survive a supremum over posterior-conditioned response couplings.

method_exemplars.technique: Use finite canonical-SCM completeness to replace unrestricted discrete mechanisms by a compact response-program mass polytope.
method_exemplars.why_closest: It supplies the lossless finite geometry over which the sharp conditional endpoints and martingale family are indexed.

method_exemplars.technique: Adapt exponential-compensator and self-normalized martingale arguments to random predictable scales.
method_exemplars.why_closest: Vanishing response masses make posterior normalization the central obstacle; the new work is uniformizing that machinery over the response polytope.

open_problems.open_problem: Resolve the full two-dimensional binary face generated by one synchronizer and two permutation response mechanisms: prove a T-independent root-T expected-width bound throughout its parameter square or exhibit a legal T-dependent interior selection with divergent normalized width.

impose a common response-table law across stages

open_problems.why_unsolved: The dynamic-IV proposal isolates the nonrectangular fact that one unit carries one response map across histories, while the Shapley proposal avoided the analogous issue by allowing distinct response laws over time. On each one-dimensional edge of the synchronizer/permutation face, endpoint linearity and scalar Abel-Doob or derivative-energy arguments may suffice, but the hidden-filter recursion is jointly nonlinear in the two mixture weights. Near permutation corners, a record-dependent interior maximizer can concentrate two-parameter derivative energy even though all nominal transition cells stay positive. The first new step is a genuinely two-parameter martingale-covering or Abel-Doob argument with proved corner integrability.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: A theorem bounding the expected supremum of the explicit two-parameter binary recursion by C sqrt(T) for every T and returning exact attaining response programs, or a fully specified legal parameter sequence with a factual-law calculation for which the supremum divided by sqrt(T) diverges.

writing_exemplar.why: Its response-coupling formulation makes this low-dimensional face a causal compatibility stress test rather than an abstract empirical-process example.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: Sharp one-step response couplings are known -> one latent unit must reuse a common response program through feedback -> the smallest interior face decides whether edgewise root-T control globalizes

method_exemplars.technique: Build exponential supermartingales after deriving a valid predictable scale for the full two-parameter family, then prove a self-normalized maximal bound.
method_exemplars.why_closest: A T-independent constant must control a record-adaptive martingale supremum as mixture weights approach a response-polytope face boundary.

method_exemplars.technique: Encode the binary mechanisms as an attainable compatible response-function face and decode optimizers into legal SCMs.
method_exemplars.why_closest: The kill-test triangle is exactly a low-dimensional compatible-response face whose endpoint laws must remain causally attainable.

open_problems.open_problem: Characterize and compute attained exact finite-record endpoints for the conditional target-policy average reward under one stationary iid response-program law, and determine exactly when they equal values from rectangular per-time response-row optimization.

open_problems.why_unsolved: Lally, Kazemi, and Paoletti prove sharpness transition by transition, but rectangular assembly can choose different admissible couplings at different times. A stationary iid-response SCM instead reuses one response-program mass vector, imposing cross-time equality constraints. Generic canonical-SCM polynomial optimization remains sharp but is expensive and does not exploit this repeated structure. The prior compiler review identifies the precise hazard: duplicating a response selector across hidden branches silently permits different SCMs in different summands. The first proof step is a shared-selector HMM/filter circuit or quotient that preserves every repeated incidence constraint and proves that each optimizer decodes to one compatible stationary SCM.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: A finite-dimensional LP, semialgebraic face formula, or exact dynamic program whose extrema equal the finite-record conditional reward endpoints, with algebraic certificates, explicit attaining response programs, and necessary-and-sufficient conditions for equality with rectangular interval-MDP bounds.

writing_exemplar.why: It cleanly motivates why nominal transitions leave same-unit response coupling ambiguous and makes the rectangular comparator explicit.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: Nominal transitions identify only response marginals -> local compatible couplings give sharp one-step bounds -> per-time recombination may be jointly unattainable -> optimize one stationary response program over the full factual record

method_exemplars.technique: Canonicalize finite discrete SCM response types and express sharp counterfactual bounds as exact polynomial programs.
method_exemplars.why_closest: The finite-record endpoint is an extremum over a canonical response-law fiber; stationarity adds repeated-variable structure absent from the generic program.

method_exemplars.technique: Use optimizer-preserving probabilistic-circuit transformations with a legal sum/max order and backtracked assignments.
method_exemplars.why_closest: The endpoint compiler must sum hidden paths while maximizing one shared response assignment, matching the structural sum-before-max constraint.

method_exemplars.technique: Construct estimators and asymptotic limit theory for optimized sharp robust policy-value endpoints.
method_exemplars.why_closest: Once the stationary-response endpoint program is known, this is the nearest dynamic policy-value template for an estimation and inference rung.

open_problems.open_problem: Construct an explicit honest simultaneous confidence fiber for both sharp conditional average-reward endpoints when the nominal controlled transition law is estimated from independent multinomial calibration samples, uniformly over zero response masses and endpoint-active face changes.

open_problems.why_unsolved: Generic partial-identification inference covers projections of moment-defined sets, and the finite-plate proposal proves the elementary union-inclusion principle once an exact multinomial region is supplied. The closest trajectory-conditioned SCM proposal was nevertheless criticized for leaving its rowwise confidence polytope and joint endpoint algorithm abstract. Here calibration uncertainty moves both the compatible-response constraints and the factual-conditioning denominators; endpoint maps kink when the active response face changes, while legal response masses may be zero. The first proof step is to invert one simultaneous multinomial region before optimization and establish deterministic inclusion of every true stationary response fiber, not differentiate a selected optimizer.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: A computable random interval obtained by projecting the union of exact stationary response fibers over a specified simultaneous transition-law confidence region, with finite-sample or uniform asymptotic 1-alpha coverage of both sharp endpoints and an explicit calibration-driven excess-diameter bound uniform in factual length T.

writing_exemplar.why: It separates coverage of a target projection from coverage of the entire identified parameter set and frames calibration as constrained endpoint optimization.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: The causal target is interval identified -> calibration makes its compatibility constraints random -> optimizer differentiation fails at face changes -> project a jointly covered transition-law fiber onto counterfactual reward

method_exemplars.technique: Calibrate relaxed sample constraints jointly and extremize the target over the resulting projected feasible set.
method_exemplars.why_closest: The desired interval is a projection of a random compatibility fiber with potentially multiple endpoint optimizers.

method_exemplars.technique: Use support-function and Hausdorff-convergence arguments for random identified sets.
method_exemplars.why_closest: The excess-diameter claim is a stability theorem for a random compatible-response set and its two one-dimensional support values.

method_exemplars.technique: Optimize finite-SCM counterfactual queries over all canonical response distributions compatible with supplied laws.
method_exemplars.why_closest: This is the population sharp-fiber operation that must be repeated over each transition law retained by the confidence region.

open_problems.open_problem: For deterministic or coarsened observation maps, characterize the observability condition separating expected root-T contraction of the same-unit counterfactual reward interval from persistent ambiguity, without assuming contraction of every conditional counterfactual kernel.

source_refs.claim: Exponential HMM filter forgetting follows from coupling conditions on posterior kernels that arbitrary deterministic observation maps need not satisfy.
source_refs.author: Randal Douc, Eric Moulines, Ya'Acov Ritov

open_problems.why_unsolved: POMDP counterfactual work generally selects a specific causal mechanism, whereas nonlinear-filter stability compares posterior state laws within one fixed hidden-state model. Here posterior uncertainty ranges over response programs, the observation map may be deterministic and non-injective, and the target is the diameter of an optimized causal reward functional. Classical emission positivity and kernel mixing therefore do not apply automatically. The first transferable step is posterior merging under an observability metric; it must be replaced by a response-polytope argument that controls only reward-relevant Poisson equivalence classes. This boundary question also enforces the topic's warning that expected shrinkage must not be upgraded to recordwise shrinkage without a new assumption.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: A matched sufficient-and-necessary theorem stated in terms of the observation map and reward-relevant response-program equivalence classes, proving C/sqrt(T) expected contraction on the detectable side and constructing a legal positive-transition nonshrinking example on the other side, without asserting shrinkage for every record.

writing_exemplar.why: It frames the practical need for individual trajectory counterfactuals under partial observability and foregrounds mechanism nonidentification.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: A factual POMDP path invites a same-unit policy question -> stochastic dynamics leave multiple SCM explanations -> a chosen mechanism gives one answer -> robust conclusions require knowing which coarsenings contract the full compatible answer set

method_exemplars.technique: Adapt the observability-to-filter-stability proof based on separation of observation laws and uniform approximation, replacing full posterior distance by a reward-relevant response functional.
method_exemplars.why_closest: Both problems ask when a long coarsened record erases latent ambiguity without stability of the underlying signal kernel.

method_exemplars.technique: Adapt posterior-kernel coupling and explicit forgetting coefficients to conditional response-program fibers.
method_exemplars.why_closest: It supplies a constructive sufficient-condition proof whose failure under deterministic coarsening can guide the negative example.

method_exemplars.technique: Use bridge-function identification and efficient POMDP off-policy estimation as a template for estimating a reward-relevant latent functional rather than the full hidden law.
method_exemplars.why_closest: The proposed frontier likewise needs only enough observability to recover or tightly bound a causal policy-value functional.

literature_map:
Balke and Pearl (1994, UAI) introduced response-function optimization for counterfactual bounds when observable conditionals do not identify mechanisms.
Tian and Pearl (2000, AMAI) derived sharp attributional-counterfactual bounds and showed how extra assumptions change them.
Zhang, Tian, and Bareinboim (2022, ICML; arXiv:2110.05690) proved finite canonical-SCM completeness for discrete counterfactual laws and reduced sharp bounds to polynomial programs.
Zaffalon et al. (2024, IJAR; arXiv:2307.08304) mapped partially specified SCMs to credal networks, established severe exact-computation complexity, and motivated query-specific optimization.
Oberst and Sontag (2019, ICML; arXiv:1905.05824) exposed SCM nonidentification for a known finite MDP, then selected the Gumbel-Max mechanism for individual counterfactual trajectories.
Lorberbom et al. (2021, NeurIPS; arXiv:2111.06888) made the mechanism-as-coupling viewpoint explicit and showed that level-2-equivalent mechanisms can optimize different counterfactual criteria.
Buesing et al. (2019, ICLR; arXiv:1811.06272) and Tsirtsis, De, and Gomez-Rodriguez (2021, NeurIPS) use selected SCMs for finite-horizon counterfactual policy search, not sharp all-mechanism intervals.
Lally, Kazemi, and Paoletti (2026, AAMAS; arXiv:2502.13731) are the closest destination paper: they give tight one-step counterfactual transition bounds and construct an interval CFMDP, but do not study one shared stationary response law or long-record contraction.
Van Handel (2009, Annals of Applied Probability; arXiv:0804.2885) links observability to nonlinear-filter stability, while Douc, Moulines, and Ritov (2009, EJP; arXiv:0712.0285) derive forgetting through posterior-kernel coupling; arbitrary deterministic coarsening need satisfy neither route.
Glynn and Infanger (2023, Stochastic Systems) clarify Poisson solutions and martingale structure for Markov-chain CLTs.
Sayedana, Caines, and Mahajan (2025, JMLR; arXiv:2411.18551) derive fixed-MDP average-reward concentration from a Poisson/fixed-point martingale decomposition; the missing step here is a maximal inequality uniform over posterior-conditioned response couplings.
Bennett et al. (2024, NeurIPS; arXiv:2404.00099) obtain sharp robust-MDP value bounds and efficient asymptotically normal endpoint estimators, but for multiplicative environment perturbations rather than same-unit mechanism fibers.
Beresteanu and Molinari (2008, Econometrica), Stoye (2009, Econometrica), and Kaido, Molinari, and Stoye (2019, Econometrica; arXiv:1601.00934) provide the closest set-valued and calibrated-projection inference machinery; none treats history-dependent fractional endpoints with zero response masses.
